object: Rude altar approximately square, but corners much rounded, 25 cm. x 33 cm., including spout
lines_described: one line of late writing round the edge
rendering: [O Wêsh!] O Ashêri! . . . : truly born of . . . ye : truly begotten of Keyañ (?).

changes.why: The group of strokes joined to a 4 is the y-i ligature seen in soreyi on Faras 6, 7, 8 and 9; Griffith renders Ashêri.
The crossed sign has the form of the ñ of Keyañ in row 3, not of the d in tedḫe in row 2.
The dark trace at the right end of the long hatched stretch cannot be read; counted as one more lost sign.
Griffith renders 'truly born of' (tedḫeli tedḫelowi, as 'truly begotten of' is terike[li teri]kelowi); the small curved mark between te and d is taken as part of the damaged d.
Griffith reads Keyañ (?): the long-tailed sign is k and the small S before it e, not the two halves of a; the crossed sign is ñ, not d.
Griffith: 'The letters kp or ke (?) following'; the long-tailed sign is k, the Σ-shaped one p (or e).

unsure.why: Name of the deceased lost: two dots, one crossed sign, then hatching with a trace.
Long hatched stretch; count estimated from the sign width of the row; a dark barred trace at its right end.
After e a hatched sign with a Z-like trace, then two dots for lost signs; Griffith gives only '. . . ye'.
Both signs hatched; a small curved stroke stands between them.
Griffith gives kp or ke (?); the second sign is Σ-shaped without the long tail of k.
Count estimated from sign width.

notes: Altar with one line round the edge, copied in four rows. Read in the order of Griffith's raised numbers 1-7: row 1, row 2, row 3, row 4, each right to left. Row 4 (kp or ke) is, per Griffith, probably the beginning of a line down the middle of the spout. No dividers are drawn; spaces follow gaps in the copy. Small dots over the first te of row 3, over the e after it and over ḫ in row 2 are not transcribed. Griffith's 'truly' answers the doubled forms tedḫeli tedḫelowi and terike[li teri]kelowi. [wosi], [re] and [li teri] are his restorations in the copy.

object: Altar, oblong, 31 cm. x 23 cm. 5, including spout
lines_described: One line of late writing round edge, worn.
first: (1)wosi : (2)soreyi a(3)l?m?ete[.]?i?s?y?w? : q?yoe : (4)terikelowi : s kidye : tedḫelo(5)wi : (8)n?[.][.]i? [.][.]q? k?soso (6)at mẖo : psḫ(7)to[.][.]
final: (1)wosi : (2)soreyi a(3)tmetel?i?qe? : mloye : (4)terikelowi : s kidye : tedḫelo(5)wi : a?[.][.] [.]m?ẖ?o psoẖo? (6)at mẖo : psḫ(7)r?[.][.]
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! At-meteli : begotten of Malêye : born of Shakizaye. (Formulae A B.)

changes.why: Griffith At-meteli, with '-qe at the end of the first name': the hook after a is t (not l); the hatched sign under his printed ? is l; the 3 with strokes is q and the last hatched sign e.
Griffith Malêye: the 3 is m and the slanting hook l (not one sign q); the four strokes are o and y.

Formulae A B: this is formula A, before at mẖo of B, with the mhê that Griffith notes for no. 6 (p. 647). The raised mark at the right end is his '?' over a sign (same shape as the ? over l in row 1), not a number 8; the long-tailed sign is the a; ξ is p (pšê); the 3 with the long tail is ẖ.
The last word of B is of the psḫ-rkete type (Griffith p. 648); the wide hooked sign is taken as r, the dot under it not as the dot of to.

kept.why: Same signs, but the copy leaves a clear gap after s (perhaps a corner of the altar); the space is kept.

unsure.why: l is hatched and carries Griffith's ?; i and e are hatched; q is a 3 with two strokes to its left.
The long stroke stands left of the three short ones; o and y are read in Griffith's order.
Mostly hatched; the sign under Griffith's ? and the long-tailed sign are taken together as a.

unsure.could_be: the last stroke the start of a lost te
unsure.why: A single stroke ends the group before at.
Wide hooked sign with a dot below it.

notes: Altar with one line round the edge, copied in three rows. Order by Griffith's numbers: row 1 (1-3); row 2 right half (4: father Malêye with terikelowi); row 2 left half (5: mother Shakizaye with tedḫelowi); then row 3 from its right end (formula A, still part 5) to (6) at mẖo (formula B) and (7). The father is named before the mother, as in his rendering. Hatched stretches at the end of row 3 counted by sign width.

object: Altar, 35 cm. x 34 cm. 5, including spout
lines_described: Two lines of late inscription round the border.
first: (1)wosi : (2)sor[e](3)yi : ry?i?d?t(4)yem?y? wi : d?okeiñ? : (5)tedḫl?owi : se(6)l?ekiye? [:] (7)y?ol? teri(8)kelowi : (9)at mẖe : (10)yl?w?rkete?[.][.] (11)[.][.]a?t? mẖe : yi?s?ke(12)te : s?m?or : l?[.](13)l?owi (14)te?o?v?eñ?w?
final: (1)wosi : (2)sor[e](3)yi : yidt(4)yeqo wi : doketeñ : (5)tedḫlowi : se(6)lekiye [:] (7)ye teri(8)kelowi : (9)at mẖe : (10)yeḫrkete?[.][.] (11)[.][.]t? mẖe : yiẖke(12)te : ssor : lḫ?(13)lowi (14)qoreñl
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! Yizataye : born of Zêketêñ : begotten of Salekiye. (Formulae B A.) Great shashêr : qêreñ.

changes.why: Griffith Yizataye: the first group is the y-i ligature (joined strokes and a 4), not r; the 3 with strokes after ye is q + o, the affix -qo(wi) (cf. his note on -qe in no. 6).
Griffith Zêketêñ: d o k e, then a 4 with a long bar (te), then ñ; see kept for te against his tê.
Griffith 'born of'; the single small sign between ḫ and o has the l form of this hand.
Griffith Salekiye (S, not Sh: the se sign).
The three strokes are one y (as in Telêye on no. 8) and the small S is e, as in the ye before rikelo on no. 9.
Griffith p. 648: ye-ḫrkete in no. 7 (formula B): the small S is e, the hooked loop ḫ.
No clear a in the hatched group; the dot after it is the dot of t.
Formula A with initial yi for pšê in no. 7 (Griffith p. 647); the 3 is ẖ.
Griffith shashêr.
Griffith 'Great' (-lakh = lḫ); the hatched sign taken as ḫ; then the ending -lowi.
Griffith qêreñ, and his note that the inscription ends abruptly with l.

kept.why: The fifth sign is a 4 with a long bar, the te form of this hand; it has nothing of the to sign (ب with a dot below).

unsure.could_be: tedḫelowi with e or l lost
unsure.why: Only one small sign stands between ḫ and o.
Small S after three strokes; Griffith does not render this element between Salekiye and terikelowi.
te partly hatched; two dots above the hatched stretch after it; two signs estimated.
Start of formula A hatched; a dot after the hatching.
Hatched; read from Griffith's 'Great'.
Drawn as a loop on an upright beside Griffith's end bar; read l from his note.

notes: Altar with two lines round the border, copied in four rows; the raised numbers 1-14 mark the parts and run right to left, row by row. Formulae B then A (Griffith p. 647). [e] and [:] are Griffith's restorations in the copy. 'end' and the upright bar after the last sign are Griffith's marks, not signs.

object: Altar, very thick, 33 cm. x 39 cm. including the spout
lines_described: One line of late inscription on border.
final: (1)wosi : (2)soreyi : (3)atmlo y[e]qo : (4)wi : sedemiye tedḫ(5)el?owi : teloye[.][.](sic)?e(6)rikelo(7)[.][.] (8)ato me p[.][.](9)ẖte : (10)a?[.][.][.][.][.][.]p?[.][.](11)ḫr
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! At-malêy[e] : born of Sazemiye : begotten of Telêye. (Formulae A B.)

changes.why: Griffith At-malêy[e]: the S after m is l (e/l confusion), the three strokes are y, the hatched sign is his restored [e], and the 3 with strokes is q + o (affix -qo).
Griffith Sazemiye: the joined 4 and 3 are m then i, the three strokes y.
Griffith Telêye: the S after te is l; the strokes are one y.
Griffith p. 647: 'erikelê for begotten in nº 8/6'.
Formula A (Formulae A B); the hook after a is t (engravers confuse l and t).
A's third group pšê-ẖte (Griffith p. 647); the 3 with the long tail to the lower left is ẖ.
Formula B (at mẖe ... ḫrkete type): the first long-tailed sign is the a, the Σ-shaped one p; the stroke and dot after r are not read.

unsure.why: The hatched sign is unreadable; e is Griffith's restoration in his rendering, not in the copy.
l hatched with a trace.

unsure.could_be: one lost sign, or a lost t (terikelo)
unsure.why: Griffith prints 'sic?' over the hatched place and calls erikelê not quite certain.
Hatched with a loop trace; the end of -lowi expected.
Only one 3-shaped sign before e.
Long hatched stretches, counts estimated; a stroke and a dot follow r.

notes: Altar with one line on the border, copied in four rows; order by Griffith's numbers 1-11, each row right to left. The divider between qo and wi stands in the copy. 'sic?' is printed by Griffith over the hatched place before erikelo.

object: Oblong altar without projecting spout, 58 cm. x 38 cm.
lines_described: One line and part of a second of late writing round the border.
first: (1)wosi asore(2)yi : m?el?oyi(3)s?y? : te?to?sẖi : tedḫlo : swe(4)oy? : tkide : ye(5)rikelo : a(6)t mẖo : yiw?rkte (7)al? mẖo : (8)yiste
final: (1)wosi asore(2)yi : ẖeloyi(3)qo : lotosẖi : tedḫeo : swe(4)y : tkide : ye(5)rikelo : a(6)t mẖo : yiḫrkte (7)at? mẖo : (8)yimte
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! Khelêyi : born of Lêtêshakhi : begotten of Shawey-takize. (Formulae B A.)

changes.why: Griffith Khelêyi: the first 3 is ẖ; the 3 with strokes after (3) is q + o (affix -qo).
Griffith Lêtêshakhi: the barred 4 is l (as in ẖeloyi), the 6-shape with a dot is tê.
In this hand the small S is e (ẖeloyi) and l is the barred 4, so no l is written here.
Griffith Shawey: the four strokes are one y.
Griffith p. 648: yi-ḫrkte in no. 9 (formula B).
Formula A; the hook is t written like l (the introduction notes the confusion).
Griffith p. 647: initial yi for pšê, and mte for ẖte, in no. 9.

kept.why: The copy has a divider between the two parts of the name; kept.

unsure.why: One small S between ḫ and o; e and l are confused in these hands.
Three strokes and an S stand where te of terikelo is expected.
Formula A usually has ato; the sign has the l/t form.
3 with two strokes, as in the -qo of nos 7 and 8.

notes: Altar with one line and part of a second round the border, copied in four rows; order by Griffith's numbers 1-8, rows right to left. Row 4 holds formula B (right) and then A (left), Griffith's BA. No hatching or lost signs.

object: Rectangular stela, with square projection at the top, h. 45 cm., w. 29 cm.
lines_described: coarsely inscribed with nine lines of late writing between rules reaching half way down, the rules continued to the bottom of the stela.
first: (1)wosi soreyi qo? m?ei(2)sḫi lo ko?d?ib? tedḫe li te(3)dḫelo aq?eebedrklo (4)sel?q?en?lo eib el?see(5)lo tete?r? be soete?l?e? ẖ?lo(6)lo ḫerin keseto li t(7)ye??delo wisi sore(8)yi ato? s?ḫe pq?ḫ?l?ẖe(9)te at?m?ḫe ksḫwra?te?
final: (1)wosi soreyi qo mli(2)sḫi lo kdib tedḫe li te(3)dḫelo amokelbedrplo (4)sleqeñlo lib lesel(5)lo teter beqetelo mlo(6)lo ḫel?b?iñ pesetol?it?(7)yet?mdelo wisi sore(8)yi ato mḫe psoḫe?ke(9)te at mḫe psḫrkete
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! The noble (?) Malishachi : truly born of Kazib : bezarap of the amêke (akhêke?) : shaleqeñ : libalesal : teter in Beqe : malê : kin of a chelabiñ of the pesatê. O Wish! O Ashêri! (Formulae A B.)

changes.why: Griffith Malishachi: the S after m is l.
Griffith Kazib; the short upright belongs to the d.
Griffith 'bezarap of the amêke (akhêke?)': after a the 3 is m (his alternative kh) with o, the small 2 with a long base k, then e l; the last long-tailed sign is p, not k.
Griffith shaleqeñ.
Griffith libalesal (s = se): the first S is l, read before 4 and b.
Griffith 'teter in Beqe : malê': 3 with a stroke is q, -te the locative; the last group is m l o + lo.
Griffith 'kin of a chelabiñ of the pesatê': the ligature after e is read l, b, i; the long-tailed sign is p; the dark sign is t and the upright curved stroke m of yetmde.
Formula A; mḫe as Griffith notes for no. 10; after p the 3 and stroke are s o, the long-tailed 3 is k.
Formula B: the Σ-shaped sign with long tail is p, the ω is r, the 2 with long tail k, then e te.

kept.why: The copy has a dotted hook (t) after peseto-li that the rendering does not account for; kept.
Same signs; the gaps of the copy are kept as spaces.

unsure.why: Griffith's 'The noble (?)'; a 3 with two strokes before the name.
One ligature of a hooked stroke, a ν-shape and a 4; l is not written apart.
The sign after to is a 5-shape with a long top bar joined to a 4; then a dotted hook.
Dark, blotted sign.
Small S joined to the tail of k.
The copy spaces almost every pair of signs; only the clearer gaps are written as spaces.

notes: Stela with nine lines; Griffith's raised numbers 1-9 are the line numbers. Copied in seven rows, each read right to left. No dividers: words end in -lo and are separated by gaps. The invocation is repeated before the formulae (wisi soreyi; 'O Wish!' in the rendering), as Griffith notes on p. 647. A row of five dots stands above the left group of row 3 (over sleqeñlo); not transcribed.

object: Rectangular stela, oblong, lower end irregular, w. 39 cm. 5, h. 30 cm. 5
lines_described: inscribed with eight lines of late writing.
final: (1)wosi : [.][.][.][.]eyi : (2)kditryeqo(3)wi kd?iye : ted(4)ḫelo[w]i : ye(5)to(sic)ẖeter : te[ri](6)kelowi : ato?(7)mẖe : [p]so[.][.][.]te[.] (8)at : m?ẖ?[.][.][.][.][.][.]
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! Kazitaraye : born of Kaziye (?) : begotten of Yetêkheter. (Formulae A B.)

changes.why: Griffith Kazitaraye; the 3 with a stroke after it is q of the affix -qowi.
Griffith Kaziye (?): the hooked 7-like sign is d, the three strokes y, the small S e.
Griffith Yetêkheter: the sign under his 'sic' is tê (to) with its dot; the 3 is ẖ, the small S e, the barred 4 with a stroke te.
The hatched sign shows a bar with a dot below, the to of formula A.
Two 3-shaped traces at the start of the hatching fit mẖe of formula B.

unsure.why: Hatched with traces at both ends; four signs estimated from width.
The d is a 7-like hook; Griffith also marks the name (?).
Hatched sign with a bar and a dot.
Griffith says at is never separated from mhe, but the copy shows a divider; then about eight hatched signs with traces.

notes: Stela with eight lines; Griffith's raised numbers 1-8 are the line numbers. Copied in four rows, each read right to left. [w], [ri] and [p] are his restorations in the copy; 'sic' over the to of Yetêkheter is his. Dotted stretch in row 4: three dots between so and te, one after te. Formulae A then B.
